hypotheses.reasoning: The notif-worker ran normally until 20:16:51 (#106). Then it hit a fatal error on msg-223156 at offset 479309: 'RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded at expandReferences' (#107). This points to a message with self-referential or very deeply nested references. The offset is never committed, so after each restart the worker goes back to 479309 (#111, #118) and crashes on the same message again (#112, #120). The restart backoff grows each time (#108, #113, #121), which is CrashLoopBackOff. Consumer lag keeps climbing (#125, #158, #204). No other service logged an error, there is no deploy, and the worker version is the same before and after the crashes.

A recent change to expandReferences in v4.19.7 could have removed a recursion guard. But this version processed batches normally before the bad message arrived, and the logs show no deploy, so this is unlikely.

verdict.recommendedAction: To get notif-worker running again, move msg-223156 (offset 479309) to a dead-letter queue, or commit past that offset, then let the backlog drain. To stop this happening again: add cycle detection or a depth limit to expandReferences, and catch per-message errors and send the message to a DLQ instead of exiting the process. Also find out which producer created the self-referential payload.
